Chapter 8: Navigating Differences—Desire, Arousal, and Relationship Dynamics
Even when you and your partner are great at communicating and staying mindful, you’re still going to run into differences—especially when it comes to desire and arousal. And you know what? That’s totally normal. These differences aren’t just something to get through; they can actually help you grow closer and understand each other better.
Desire discrepancies—like when one person wants sex more often, or less often, than the other—are incredibly common. The dual control model gives us a little insight here: every person has their own unique mix of accelerators and brakes. These are shaped by things like stress, context, and past experiences.
So instead of thinking, “We’ve got a problem,” what if you approached these differences with genuine curiosity and kindness? Here are a few ways you can do that:
First, normalize variation. Our desire ebbs and flows—that’s just part of being human.
Second, focus on connection. Even when your desire levels aren’t perfectly in sync, you can still nurture emotional and physical intimacy.
Third, try exploring responsive desire. Sometimes, you might not feel desire right away, but getting close through affectionate touch or shared activities can spark it.
And finally, don’t be afraid to negotiate and compromise. Maybe you try scheduling intimate time, or find new ways to connect that work for both of you.
Now, let’s talk about relationship dynamics. Things like power imbalances, old arguments, or even little resentments can act like brakes, slowing down desire. If you notice these patterns, having honest conversations—or even working with a therapist—can help rebuild trust and bring back intimacy.
Here’s a real-life example: imagine a couple where one partner wants sex more often than the other. Instead of letting that become a sore spot, they decide to focus on nonsexual closeness—like cuddling or picking up a hobby together. Over time, that takes the pressure off, and desire starts to show up in a more natural way.
So, here’s a key thing to remember: desire isn’t set in stone. It changes as life changes—becoming a parent, dealing with illness, getting older—all of these can shift the balance of those accelerators and brakes. If you stay flexible and keep supporting each other, you can navigate whatever comes your way, together.
